name: Affiliate Management
body:
User Manual for  Affiliate Management App

1. Introduction 2. Installation 3. Configuration 4. Becoming an Affiliate5. Managing Affiliates6. Affiliate Tools7. Reporting and Commission Management


1. Introduction 

The Odoo Affiliate Management module allows you to set up and manage an affiliate program within your Odoo environment. This manual will guide you through the installation, configuration, and usage of the module.

2. Installation 

Follow these steps to install the Odoo Affiliate Management module:

  1. Download and extract the zip file containing the module.
  2. Locate the 'affiliate_management' folder in the extracted files.
  3. Copy this folder to your Odoo Add-Ons directory on the server.
  4. Open your Odoo instance and navigate to Settings.
  5. Activate the Developer Mode.
  6. Go to the Apps menu and click on "Update Modules List".
  7. Search for "affiliate_management" in the search bar (remove all filters).
  8. Click "Install" next to the Affiliate Management module.

3. Configuration 

After installation, configure the module as follows:

1. Navigate to Menu > Affiliate Manager > Configuration > Settings.

2. Define the following details:

  • Affiliate product if desired
  • Payment day
  • Minimum payout balance
  • Email configurations
  • Enable PPC (Pay Per Click) if desired
  • Enable "Automatic Approve Request" for automated approval

3. Click on the 'Configure' button under the Affiliate Program option.

4. Set up PPC (Pay Per Click) and PPS (Pay Per Sale) rates.

5. Configure advanced computation settings for PPC and PPS if needed.

6. Save your configuration.

4. Becoming an Affiliate

For users to become affiliates:

1. Users should click on "Affiliate" under "Useful links" on their portal.

2. They will receive an email to complete the signup process.

3. Admins can view affiliate requests under Affiliate Manager > Affiliate Program > Pending Requests.

4. Approve or reject requests as needed.

5. Managing Affiliates

Once approved, affiliates can:

1. Access their affiliate account via the "View my Affiliate Account" button.

2. Check their clicks, orders, commissions earned, and other details.

6. Affiliate Tools

Affiliates can generate promotional links:

1. Click on the "TOOLS" button in the affiliate dashboard.

2. Generate affiliate links or product-specific links as needed.

7. Reporting and Commission Management

To manage affiliate activities and payouts:

1. Monitor affiliate performance through "Order Reports" and "Traffic Reports" under Affiliate Manager > Reports.

2. Process commissions:

  • For sales: Affiliate Manager > Reports > Order report > Pay Per Sale

  • For clicks: Affiliate Manager > Reports > Traffic Report > Pay Per Click

3. To pay commissions:

  • Click Pay Per Sale > Confirm > Create Invoice > Confirm Draft Bill

4. Affiliates can view their earned commissions on their affiliate dashboard.

User Manual for  SALES MODULE

User Manual for  SALES MODULECustomersCustomer CreationQuotations / Sales OrdersCash/Credit SalesProfit Margin Control in sales orders.Overdue Control in Sales Orders.Credit Limit Control in Credit Sales Orders.Bank Guarantee Control in Credit Sales Orders.Confirming the quotation:Sending a Quotation or a Pro-forma invoice.Posting the Invoice and getting the payment for the Cash Sale.Receive the PaymentDeliverySales ReturnsReturn Delivery OrderCredit note (Return Invoice)Approval for Credit NotePayment for returned items.View the Sales Return from the sales order:Journal Updates of invoices.


Customers

Navigation: Sales > Menu > Orders > Customers

Initially, the customers will be displayed in Kanban view. Click the List button to change to the List-View.

Customer Creation

Before creating a new customer, always check whether the same customer is already created. To check that, filter the customers list by the name, and then if found, verify the customer using other fields such as contact details. If the customer is not found, then a new customer can be created. This is to avoid creating duplicate records for the same customer.

·         To create a customer record, click on CREATE button and fill customer’s details as below.


·         Enter the Customer’s name & address.

·         Enter the tax ID of the customer.

·         Select the customer group. For walk-in cash customers set as “CASH”. For any other customer, initially set as “CASH” and request the Finance department to update the correct customer group.

·         Enter the contact information

The rest of the fields are in the tabs below which are to be filled.

 

Tab: Sales & Purchase


·         Sales Team: Set the sales center by which the customer is created.

·         Payment Term: For Cash Customers, set as “Immediate Payment”. For Credit Customers, this must be initially set as “Immediate Payment” and then request the Finance department to set the credit period.

·         Payment Type: For Cash Customers, set as “Cash”. For Credit Customers, initially set as Cash and request the Finance department to convert the customer as a credit customer by setting this field as “Credit”.

·         Credit Limit: The credit limit is to be set by the Finance Department. (Only for credit customers)

 

Tab: Tax Registration


·         VAT Registration Status: If the customer is VAT-Registered, then select “VAT Registered”. Otherwise, select “VAT Not Registered”. If the VAT Registration Status is selected as “VAT Registered”, then the “VAT registration Number” and “SVAT Registration Status” will appear.

·         VAT Registration Number: Enter the VAT registration number.

·         SVAT Registration Status: If the Customer is registered for “SVAT”, then select the SVAT registration status as “SVAT Registered”. If the SVAT registration status is selected as “SVAT Registered” then the “SVAT Registration Number” appears.

·         SVAT Registration Number: Enter the SVAT Registration Number.

 

Tab: Bank Guarantee Details

The Bank Guarantee amount and the expiry date are recorded in the customer's record.

For customers having customer groups in which the Group Type is not "General", the Bank Guarantee details are mandatory.

For customers having customer groups in which the Group Type is "DISTRIBUTORS", the tick box "Mandatory Bank Guarantee" will be ticked automatically. This can be changed as required.


·         Enter the Bank Guarantee Amount

·         Enter the Bank Guarantee Expiry Date.

·         Mandatory Bank Guarantee: If this field is ticked, a validation is triggered at the time of confirming or posting the invoice of a sales order. The system will check whether the bank guarantee is expired or whether the bank guarantee limit will be exceeded by posting the current order. If so, the system will not allow it to proceed with the order.

·         Bank Guarantee Docs: Upload a reference document using the UPLOAD YOUR FILE button.

 

Quotations / Sales Orders

In Odoo, a quotation or a sales order are 2 stages in the same document. Therefore a single order number will be maintained for the quotation and for the sales order which a quotation was converted to. A sale can be initiated by creating an order either as a quotation or as a sales order.

Cash/Credit Sales

Navigation: Sales > Menu > Orders > Quotations


Click CREATE.

The blank form to create a quotation will be opened.


·         Fill out the Sales Order form and save.

 

Filling the Sales Order:

·         Select the Customer
The invoice address and the delivery address will be updated automatically. For a credit sale, the credit limit must be set for the selected customer.

·         Select the Quotation Type as “Sales”.

·         Click on “Add a product” to add sales lines.         

o   Select the product. (The unit price is automatically updated according to the Price List.)

o   Enter the quantity. (The Subtotal is automatically calculated.)

o   If discounts are applicable, enter the discount percentage. It must be less than or equal to the maximum discount percentage which is set in the Items Master file. If a third part commission is to be paid, then the criteria [Discount % + Commission % =< Maximum Discount %] must be satisfied.

The totals are calculated at the bottom as and when the quantity, unit price, tax percentage, or discounts are changed.

The tab “Other Info”:


·         Payment Term: For a cash sale, select “Immediate Payment” and for a credit sale, select the correct term with the preferred credit period.

·         Set the correct warehouse that is related to the sales point.

The tab “Credit Limit Details”:


The customer’s credit details are available in this tab. This tab is relevant only for credit sales.

Over Credit: This indicates whether this sales order has exceeded the available credit balance.

Customer Credit Limit: The credit limit of the customer, which is set in the Customer master file.

Cust. Total Receivable: The total amount that the customer has to pay us.

Current Tot. Amount: The total value of the current sales order.

Over Credit Amount:  = (Total of this sale - Balance Credit)

Credit Limit Approved: This indicates whether the approval is given to proceed with the sales order in which the credit limit is exceeded, as indicated in the Over Credit field.

 

Profit Margin Control in sales orders.


In sales orders, for each item, the profit margin is validated against the minimum profit margin which is set in the system as a global parameter. In an instance where the margin does not meet at least the minimum margin, the below buttons appear. To proceed with such a sales order with the same low margin, approval is to be given by an authorized person upon a request from the sales user.

INSUFFICIENT MARGIN DETAILS: Click this button to view details of the current margin of each item and the minimum margin.

REQUEST INSUFFICIENT MARGIN APPROVAL: Click this button to request approval to proceed with the sales order. Then this button disappears and the approving button appears. Only authorized users can give approval to proceed with low margins.


·         Click APPROVE INSUFFICIENT MARGIN.

The CONFIRM button appears.

 

Overdue Control in Sales Orders.

If a customer has not paid for invoices by the due date, such a customer is considered as an overdue customer. If such a customer is selected in a sale order, the sales order cannot be proceeded unless a special approval is given by an authorized person. The user who created the sales order can request for the approval by clicking on the REQUEST OVERDUE APPROVAL button. Overdue details can be viewed by clicking on VIEW CREDIT LIMIT OVERDUE DETAILS button.


·         Click REQUEST OVERDUE APPROVAL


·         Click APPROVE OVERDUE. (This can be done only by an authorized user.)

Credit Limit Control in Credit Sales Orders.

If the customer’s balance credit amount is not sufficient for the current sale, the user is not able to proceed with the sales order unless the customer pays the due amount or special approval is given by an authorized user. If the sale is to be done with special approval, then the user has to request to give approval by using the REQUEST CREDIT LIMIT APPROVAL button.


·         Click REQUEST CREDIT LIMIT APPROVAL


·         Click APPROVE CREDIT LIMIT.
Then the system will not validate against the credit limit. Therefore the user can proceed with the sales order.

Bank Guarantee Control in Credit Sales Orders.

In an instance which the sales order is created to a distributor who’s, the bank guarantee is made mandatory, and the current sales order is going to exceed the bank guarantee limit, the user is not able to proceed with the sales order unless an approval is given by an authorized user. However if it is required to proceed with the sale, then the user who created, has to request for approval from an authorized user by using REQUEST BANK GUARANTEE APPROVAL button.


·         Click REQUEST BANK GUARANTEE APPROVAL.


·         Click APPROVE BANK GUARANTEE.

 

 

Confirming the quotation:

When a quotation is confirmed, it becomes a sales order. Both a quotation and a sales order are the same and have the same reference number, but in different stages.


The CONFIRM button disappears and the CREATE INVOICE button appears.

 

Sending a Quotation or a Pro-forma invoice.

A quotation or a Pro-forma invoice can be directly sent to the customer by email as a PDF file attachment using the below buttons.


·         SEND BY EMAIL: Click to send a quotation.

·         SEND PRO-FORMA INVOICE: Click to send a pro-forma invoice.


·         Do any modification if required and click SEND to send the email.

The email will be sent to the customer as a PDF attachment. The email address is the one set in the customer record. But it can be changed at the time of sending the email in the above screen and any additional emails can be added if required.

 

Posting the Invoice and getting the payment for the Cash Sale.

At the head office, the payment is received by the cashier.

·         Retrieve the sales order.

o   Sales > Orders > Sales Orders

o   Filter by the order number and open the sales order.


·         Click on CREATE INVOICE.


·         Select the appropriate option (Regular invoice/Down payment %/Down payment (fixed amount)) based on how the payment is received. For a Cash sale, leave the “Regular invoice” selected. For partial invoices, select one of the “Down payment….” options.

·         Click CREATE AND VIEW INVOICE.

An invoice is created in draft mode and the created invoice is opened.


·         Click on CONFIRM to post the invoice

The posted Invoice:


·         If the invoice is to be sent by email click SEND & PRINT. The invoice can be sent directly through Odoo.


·         To print the invoice click on “Print” icon and select “Invoice”. The invoice will be downloaded to the computer as a PDF file. Then it can be printed or sent as an attachment through the email application (Outlook).

Receive the Payment

Note: For cash sales the payment must be received before the dispatch of goods. Therefore immediately after the invoice posting at the cashier, the payment must be received. For credit sales, the payment receiving process is skipped and goods are dispatched and the payment is received later using the same method described here.

·         During a cash sale, the posted invoice may be already in the screen by now. But, in the case of a credit sale, the invoice was posted some time back and, to receive the payment, the same invoice should be retrieved.
Sales > Orders > Sales Orders > filter and open the sales order > click Invoices > open the invoice.

The posted invoice is opened. The payment is received against the posted invoice.


·         Click on REGISTER PAYMENT

·         Click CREATE PAYMENT.

The payment is posted.
For credit sales, this payment receiving is done later, based on the payment term.

The Posted invoice which the payment is received:

The Invoice Stage will be “Posted” and the label “IN PAYMENT” will be displayed on the invoice.

The paid amount and the due amount are displayed at the bottom.

 

Delivery

·         Click the “Delivery” smart button.

 

The Delivery Order:

·         Select the serial numbers of products which serial numbers are assigned.
For such items, when the serial numbers are selected, the “Done” quantity is updated. For other items the “Done” quantity can be typed manually; or else the total pending quantity can be instantly set using the SET QUANTITY button.

·         Click SET QUANTITIES.

·         Click VALIDATE.

The Delivery Order is posted

The completed Sales Order:

Sales Returns

In Odoo the sales return is initiated from the original sales order.

Return Delivery Order

·         Retrieve the original sales order.

·         Click Delivery

The original Delivery is opened.

There are 4 item lines in the delivery. From this, we can return a selected set of items.

Example: Returning quantity 1 of the last item.

·         Click RETURN

The below screen appears allowing to remove unwanted lines and to leave the only lines which are to be returned.

·         Edit the returning quantity of the last item and remove the first two lines.

·         Click RETURN.

The Return Delivery Order is created.

Under the “Operations” tab the line to be returned is displayed with the returning quantity.

Click SET QUANTITIES.

The returning item is now displayed in the “Detailed Operations” tab with the returning quantity under “Done” column.

The return delivery order is now posted and it can be monitored in the sales order and in delivery orders.

·         Open the sales order. 2 Delivery Orders are indicated in the Delivery smart button and the Delivered quantity is reduced by one quantity.

By now the return delivery is updated and the return invoice is to be updated.

Credit note (Return Invoice)

·         Click the smart button “Invoices”.

·         Click ADD CREDIT NOTE.

·         Click REVERSE.

The draft Credit Note is created

Approval for Credit Note

·         Edit the returning quantity of the last line.

·         Remove the other two lines using the delete buttons in the right-hand corner.

·         Click REQUEST CREDIT NOTE APPROVAL.
This is done by the sales user and then the approval is to be given by an authorized user.

·         Click APPROVE CREDIT NOTE

·         Click CONFIRM.

The Credit note (Return Invoice) is posted.

 

Payment for returned items.

·         Click REGISTER PAYMENT.

·         Click CREATE PAYMENT.

The payment is posted and it is indicated as IN PAYMENT on the credit note.
The letter “R” is added at the beginning of the Credit Note (Return Invoice) number.


View the Sales Return from the sales order:

·         Open the Sales Order.

·         Click the “Delivery” smart button to see the delivery orders.
There will be 2 delivery orders. One for the original delivery and the other for the return.

·         Click Invoices Smart button to see the invoices.

·         There will be 2 invoices. One for the original invoice and the other for the credit note (Return).

Journal Updates of invoices.

·         Select one of the invoice records in the above screenshot.

·         Select the Journal Items tab.

The original invoice.

The Credit Note (Return Invoice)

 

End of the Sales Process.

name: Procedure in setting user permissions.
body:
Note: For further details, refer to the 1st article "Odoo User Access Rights".

Steps

  1. Identify all the main different functionalities of a module.
  2. Create user groups based on functionalities.
  3. Identify different users by access rights.
  4. Create sample user accounts as same as actual users in the module.
  5. Assign user groups to each user based on their duties.
  6. Configure the user groups
    1. Inherited: If there is another user group with lower access rights that has been already configured and can be inherited into the current user group, inherit them in the "Inherited" tab.
    2. Menus: For any customized menus that are to be granted permission, then add each menu into the "Menus" in the user group.
    3. Views: Get the list of Views from the lowest level user group of the model and add them to the user group that is being tested.
    4. Access Rights: Start the process with the user, who has minimum or no access rights set in any user group.
      1. ​In any event, since no access rights are given to groups, the system will give error messages. Each message will mention the model to which the access is needed and in which level and other user groups that have the required access rights.
      2. Add the model with the mentioned access level to the user group under "Access Rights".
      3. Then continue with the process.
      4. /Repeat the same using error messages
    6. Record Rules: Set record rules if sets of different records in the same model need to be controlled differently.
    7. Repeat with the next user having a different role.

7 Use the Access Management application to restrict any specific field or button to the user.

Odoo User Access Rights - System Administration Point of View

Table of Contents

Abstract ​​1. Inheritance ​2. Basic user creation ​3. User typesInternal Users ​4. Technical Groups ​5.User Access Groups ​6.Application Access Groups ​Inheritance ​Menus  ​Views ​Access Rights ​Record Rules ​7. Dual control policy / Two person control8. Default user template8.1 Default User Template Groups9.How to Create Customized User Access Group10. Sample Test case for check user access rights in Account Module user groups11. Concepts (Findings)12. Steps to follow create a new user group views for particular UAG13. Odoo Version 17 Testing & Findings13.1 Create a  specific technical group to "Product Add/Update/Delete option" userwise.         

Abstract

In this section, will discuss few concepts related to access rights in Odoo 15 and how these concepts linked to at the time of system implementation.

​​1. Inheritance


In the depicted image illustrates how inheritance works in Odoo 15.

​

The above Venn diagrams to represent the inheritance relationships between these user groups as follows.


Group A (Base User Group)

Represents the base user group without any inheritance.

Group B (Manager Group)

Inherits from Group A, meaning it has all the access and privileges of Group A.
Represents an extension of Group A, with additional access.


Group C (Executive Group)

Inherits from both Group A and Group B, meaning it has all the access and privileges of both groups.
Represents an extension of both Group A and Group B, with additional access.


​2. Basic user creation

Odoo defines a user as someone who has access to a database to perform daily tasks. You can add as many users as you need and, in order to restrict the type of information each user can access, rules can be applied. Users and access rights can be added and changed at any point.


Go to Settings -> Manage Users and click on Create.

Fill in the form with the needed information. Under the tab Access Rights choose the group within each application the user can have access to.
The list of applications shown is based on the applications installed on the database.




There are several different types of user access group:

  1. User Types (Internal, Portal, Public)
      Users must be allocated to one type. 
  2. Application access groups, for example: Inventory User, Purchase Administrator (Manager), Accountant.
  3.  ‘Technical Settings‘ access groups relate to specific functionality:
    • Manage multiple units of measure
    • Analytic accounting
  4. Extra Rights (Multi Currency, Multi Company)
  5. Other (Access to Private Addresses) 

They grant access to:

    1. Database
      1. Models
      2. Records (through Record Rules)
      3. Fields (not normally used) 
    2. Views 
    3. Menus
    4. Windows Actions
    5. Other elements (Buttons, Wizards)


User access groups “inherit” permissions from other groups. This is standard for the application access groups. For example:

​Purchase Manager inherits the Purchase User rights
​Purchase User inherits the Internal User rights


​3. User types


  1. Internal users can have full access to Odoo applications
  2. Portal users could be customers or vendors (with access only to relevant documents)
  3. Public users can only access the website



Internal Users

  1. Internal Users are almost always members of multiple application access groups (e.g. Purchase Manager and Inventory User).
  2. Internal Users will also be members of several ‘technical’ access groups, each of which has a specific purpose, for example:
    • Manage multiple units of measure
    • Analytic accounting
  3. Internal Users may also have Extra Rights (Multi Currency, Multi Company), and other access (e.g. Private Addresses). Again, these are all access groups.
  • Access from all of a user’s access groups is combined together.


​4. Technical Groups

​1. As well as application access groups, Odoo has what are called “Technical” groups. These are only ​visible on the User profile in Developer Mode.

​2. In principle, these are no different to the Application Access Groups, but they each serve a much ​more limited purpose and grant less access

​3. None of these groups have Record Rules


​4. Some Groups grant access to Views and Menus.


​5. Some don’t directly grant any access at all.



​5.User Access Groups

Purpose - Define access given to groups of users in an Odoo database.

User Access Groups define access given to groups of users in an Odoo database. They standardize and simplify user access so that setting up a user should be fairly simple.


​6.Application Access Groups

We’ll look at the access for the Sales application.

Enable Developer Mode, Navigate to Settings, select Users & Companies > Groups and set the filter to see sales groups:




Eg : There are three groups for sales

  1. Sales Administrators (Managers)
  2. Sales / User: All Documents
  3. Sales / User: Own Documents Only


​Inheritance

We can see the structure from the Inherited tab

Starting with the “Own Documents” group (lowest level for Sales)



The “Own Documents” group inherits the “Internal User” group, which provides a basic level of access. It also provides access to two related apps if they are installed: Subscriptions and Events.


​Menus 

This tab is where you define which menus (models) the user can have access to.  Note that some menus are not restricted to specific access groups.



​Views

The “Own Documents” group grants access to some views. Note that most views are available for all user access groups, and therefore this tab may be empty.

   


​Access Rights

Access Rights rules are the first level of rights. The field is composed of the object name, which is the technical name given to a model. For each model, enable the following options as appropriate:

  • Read: the values of that object can be only seen by the user.
  • Write: the values of that object can be edited by the user.
  • Create: values for that object can be created by the user.
  • Delete: the values of that object can be deleted by the user.



​Record Rules

They control which records users can access.  For example, sales users can only access their own quotations and sales orders (see below).



  • Record Rules can make it easier to develop functionality in Odoo (because the rules have already been setup)
  • However, they can cause problems if there are multiple requirements related to one Model (database table).
    • So it is possible that installing another app or module (or just enabling another feature, such as Private Addresses) can have unexpected results.


​7. Dual control policy / Two person control

Dual control, also known as two-person control or two-factor authentication, is a security measure that requires the involvement of two individuals to authorize or carry out certain actions or transactions. It is commonly used in high-security environments or sensitive operations to prevent unauthorized access, fraud, or errors.

In the context of user access rights, dual control refers to a mechanism where two authorized individuals are required to jointly perform certain actions related to user access management. This adds an additional dimension of security and ensures that no single individual can abuse their privileges or make unauthorized changes to user access rights.

There are few steps/works in user access management.

Authorization Process: When granting or modifying user access rights, the dual control mechanism requires that two authorized individuals independently review and approve the request. Each individual verifies the request and provides their authorization.

Segregation of Duties: The two individuals involved in the dual control process should have distinct roles or responsibilities. This segregation of duties ensures that no single individual can have complete control over user access rights.

Approval Workflow: The workflow for user access rights requests is designed in a way that requires both authorized individuals to provide their approval before the changes can be implemented. This can involve the use of separate accounts or credentials for each individual.

Audit Trail: All actions related to user access rights, including approvals and modifications, should be logged and recorded in an audit trail. This allows for accountability and facilitates monitoring and investigation in case of any security breaches or unauthorized changes.

8. Default user template


Settings - > General settings -> Permissions -> Default Access Rights -> Default Access Rights

This will bring up the Default User Template where you can select the default permissions for default user. Note that this template is shown as ARCHIVED; it can, and is, still applied to new users, it's just not listed as an active user. This prevents it from being accidentally modified or removed, and shall be left as 'archived'.

There will be options for each app you have installed to the database which require permissions. Not all the permissions are visible on this screenshot, so please use the scroll bar to navigate through all your available options.



N.B. As per default user template will take as benchmark for each user access rights at the time of user creation in the Odoo database. However, can change access levels depend on their demand of the other applications that user needed.


8.1 Default User Template Groups

There are few groups inherits according to this template which means any user will create these default template groups will add automatically to the new user. 

E.g : 36 Technical user groups will add to the new user.


Same time access rights and basic record rules also added to the default user as per above scenario.



9.How to Create Customized User Access Group


Go to developer mode - > Settings -> Users & companies -> Groups -> Create Group

Application - Area of the user access group belongs to

Name - Proper name for identification

Users  - intended users allocate to this group

inherited  - existing user groups access to inherit

Menus - special menu grated to this group

Views - new views to include

Access rights - special permission added 

Record rules - restrict record rules  


Eg: In Accounts application, I have added few functional areas as customized groups to get an idea.


Eg: ABCD user has already added to AccountExecutive user group and under accounting application his access look like this.


Therefore, In this situation system administrator can able to segregate special user access rights to this group ( AccountExecutive) separate from other user groups. Further, we can alter any access rights, views and any other record rules to grant/revoke access rights to the system any given time.



10. Sample Test case for check user access rights in Account Module user groups


Test Case Check List: Accounts Module User Group Access Rights in Odoo 15

10.1     Preconditions:

         Ensure the Odoo 15 instance is set up with the latest version of the accounts module.

         Create at least two different user groups with distinct access rights, e.g., "Cashier" and                                 "AccountExecutive."

10.2     Test the Create Access:

         Log in as a user with the "Cashier" group and try to create a new journal entry.

         Verify that the "Cashier" can create a new journal entry successfully.

         Log in as a user with the "AccountExecutive" group and repeat the test, verifying that the                             "AccountExecutive" can also create a new journal entry.

10.3     Test the Read Access:

         Create a few journal entries with the "Cashier" user.

         Log in as a user with the "AccountExecutive" group and attempt to view the journal entries created             by the "Cashier."

         Verify that the "AccountExecutive" can view the journal entries created by the "Cashier."

10.4     Test the Update Access:

         Create a journal entry with the "Cashier" user.

         Log in as the "AccountExecutive" user and try to edit the journal entry created by the "Cashier."

         Verify that the "AccountExecutive" can edit the journal entry.

10.5     Test the Delete Access:

         Create a journal entry with the "Cashier" user.

         Log in as the "AccountExecutive" user and attempt to delete the journal entry created by the                      "Cashier."

         Verify that the "AccountExecutive" can delete the journal entry.

10.6     Test the Restricted Access:

         Log in as a user without any special groups assigned.

         Attempt to access the accounts module and perform various actions such as create, read, update,               and delete.

·         Verify that the user without any special groups cannot access or perform any actions within the                  accounts module.

10.7     Test the Report Access:

         Log in as a user with the "Cashier" group and generate various financial reports, such as Balance                Sheet, Profit & Loss, etc.

         Verify that the "Cashier" can generate the reports successfully.

         Repeat the test with a user having the "AccountExecutive" group, ensuring they can also generate               the financial reports.

10.8     Test the Approval Process:

         Configure a journal entry approval process requiring approval from a specific group, e.g.,                             "Management_Approval."

         Log in as a user without the "Management_Approval" group and attempt to create a journal entry.

         Verify that the journal entry requires approval and cannot be posted until approved by a user with             the "Management_Approval"  group.

10.9     Test Negative Scenarios:

         Log in as a user with the "Cashier" group and try to access and perform actions in other                               unrelated modules.

         Verify that the "Cashier" user is restricted from accessing unrelated modules.

10.10  Test User Group Hierarchies:

         Create a new user group and assign it to a user, e.g., "Auditor."

         Configure the "Auditor" group to inherit some access rights from the "Cashier" group.

         Log in as the user with the "Auditor" group and perform actions within the accounts                                     module.

         Verify that the user with the "Auditor" group has access rights inherited from the                                        "Cashier" group.

10.11  Test User Group Customizations:

         Create a new user group and customize its access rights to limit or extend permissions within the               accounts module.

         Assign the new user group to a user and test various actions within the accounts module.

         Verify that the customizations to the user group's access rights are applied correctly.


11. Concepts (Findings)


Internal User Group

Any newly developed model is automatically added in to this group "Internal user", under the  "Access Rights" tab.

Since any user is included in this user group by default, any user will get access to all the models in this group. 

Therefore, under the "Access Rights" tab, remove access of all the unrequired models in this user group "Internal User". ( Depend on the user access models)

Internal User Group

Add access rights models (" ir.model " / label - "models" Read Access only) to this internal user group to support to other models as well as minimize to access other common modules such as e-mail marketing user.

Inheritance



Accounts Module

1. Create a User Group (No access rights required under the tab "Access Rights".)  (Example:  "Test - Inheritance")

2. Set the application as "Accounting", which is the 2nd record having the name "Accounting" with a description.

3. Set inheritance according to the required order in the dropdown list of the field "Accounting" under the user's setup.




Sales Module

1. Create a User Group (No access rights required under the tab "Access Rights".)  (Example:  "Test - Sales Inheritance - Min Rights")

2. Set the application as "Sales", which is the 1st record having the name "Sales" with a description.

3. Set inheritance according to the required order in the dropdown list of the field "Sales" under the user's setup.


Conclusion

In Sales, the inheritance must be done according to the required order.

If this inheritance is not properly set, the whole section with the set of user groups will go down in the user's setup screen.

Then the Dropdown list disappears and each user group will be displayed separately.



12. Steps to follow create a new user group views for particular UAG


1. Activate developer mode


2. Get a copy of base system UAG ( Eg: if you are create a new user group to resctrict access rights for purchase module, then duplicate a purchase application base level user group of " Purchase/User " ) with proper name. The idea behind that it will copied all the componenets such as users,inherited,menu,views, access rights, record rules etc..



3. After that remove the inherited user groups, access rights as you wish since we are mainly regulate particular model create/delete/read access rights respectively. However, views are more sensitive than access rights since it will share number of models as well as some base system functionalities to run the system procedures. Therefore, if particular user group unable to access mandatory view then it will diffucult to simulate with user access rights. Keep in mind that always compare that base level user group views and your own user group views with their names and its functionalies before it add/remove vice versa.


13. Odoo Version 17 Testing & Findings


  • Enhanced access with improved UI for managing security settings. further, minimum access level/group will show administrator to when setting particular user access rights to maintain minimum base user group for each application wise. Refer below example.


13.1 Create a  specific technical group to "Product Add/Update/Delete option" userwise.         


In Odoo 17 most of the users belongs to purchase,inventory and account have access to create product option. Therefore we have to restrict product creation part only to specific users specially in warehouse. To segreate production creation right we have to follow below steps for your reference.

Identify the technical model which belongs to product and product variation right access groups firstly. Check in produt.produt and produt.template respectively.



Select product.template and go to access rights tab

Most of the groups have to create,write , delete access. Same as product.product model as well. Therefore, we have to restrict access from above groups and same as we have to grant our own access group to CRUD. like our own group under technical " Product Create/Edit/Delete" and provide rights as per our own wish.



Same way add both models to above new technical group to product.template and product.product respectively.

After we have to add respective users who need access rights create product add that special technical option to on of off. new option will display at the bottom of the each user edit view. enable it as when required. This way administrator can safe guard product modification access rights in Odoo base product from unnecessary user groups.

Repair Module – Configuration Documentation

Administration User Point of View                              

Table of Contents

How to create a Helpdesk TeamRepair TypesHelpdesk StagesRepair Reason


How to create a Helpdesk Team

Purpose - Create customer service method based on the ticket system

The Help Desk module basically works based on a ticket system. Customer's queries will be registered as tickets and the company can take required action on each ticket within a specified time. In Odoo, tickets can be registered in the Helpdesk module automatically with the help of various platforms. A customer can submit queries through Email, Live Chat, phone calls, and website forms. The Helpdesk module ensures direct conversion of recorded queries into tickets and assigns them to different helpdesk teams. It is also possible to register tickets directly in the Helpdesk module.

To create a new helpdesk team first of all go to helpdesk app and go to configuration and click on helpdesk team option.

Helpdesk -> Configuration -> helpdesk teams

 

Name – Proper name for helpdesk

Select the Assignment model

                Manual – User has provision to assign the desk

                Random – Odoo will automatically assign

                Balanced – Least amount of tickets desk system will assign

Repair Types

Purpose – to create a list of repair categories

To create list of repair types go to helpdesk application configuration tab.

Helpdesk -> Configuration -> Types

 


Name – Name of the repair type

RUG/with serial No/without serial no – tick to correct type

RUG (Repair under Guarantee) – In this type need to approved by higher management as well as item fault must be defect of the item as well as issue should not be customer fault. After sales item must be less than one year with sold date.  

Repair under Warranty - External not RUG - This type also fallen into under warranty category but RUG approval not granted due to root cause of the pump not related to technical/manufacture. Therefore, customer has to pay repair cost as well as raw materials estimated cost.

With Serial Number – This category fault item has a unique serial number and it must be more than one year old item.

Without serial Number – under this category difficult to find out serial number from the item itself as well as from company records as well. In this situation repair item assign to this category and Odoo system will generate new serial number for the item and later it will help to retrieve the information.

 

 

Helpdesk Stages

Purpose – to maintain stages of the ticketing system

In a ticketing system repair status can be different from time to time. After initiate new ticket for repair job user has to update the current status according to ongoing job situation. E.g.:  For RUG job first thing assign a new ticket number then move to “Approval for RUG” status until to get the management approval. Then if it is ok only move to the “in progress” stage and so on.



 


Repair Reason


Purpose - Maintain list of root causes related to defect pump

These are common root causes belongs pump repair reasons. Therefore, when an repair item may have one or more reasons depend on its root cause. System user can set up these reasons as parameters.

Recruitment Process

Human Resource management module and recruitment process in version 15 is another important app of Odoo ERP software. Recruitment module is important function of any organization as it manages selecting proper candidate that offers you with proper talent recruited for the position. Odoo recruitment process helps you with better planning, proper selection & decision making for the employees you would be hiring for your business processes.

Odoo recruitment process offers you to understand the job vacancies in your company, analysis of the job requirements, application reviews, screening of employee, short listing, and finalization of right candidate for the position. How can we handle the perfect recruitment process?

An efficient organization is always oriented towards or is focused with a bull’s eye on the recruitment process with a specific sourcing model that intents the right time to right fit for the right job. This step-by-step process is perfectly handled by the Odoo 15. Usually, an all-inclusive recruitment process takes place with seven different phases. It differs with company management, size and structure of the organization, the workflow of the company, nature of the operations of work, and so on. The seven phases of recruitment are identifying the hiring needs, preparing and posting the job description as per the requirements, searching for the right candidate with the talents or skills, screening and shortlisting the candidates, Interviewing the

executives, evaluating the availability of the candidates and passing the contract, orientation and introduction of the new employee to the organization and team members.   • How to Activate the Lots & Serial Numbers in the System

Serial numbers can be assigned to each product in inventory. In the inventory module, you can activate the 'Lots & Serial Numbers' option under the Product Traceability field in the Settings menu. After enabling this field, you will get the Lots & Serial Numbers option under the Products menu in the Inventory module.

  • How to Activate the Storage Locations and Multi Step Routes in the System

​Odoo manages three types of locations which are Physical Locations, Partner Locations and Virtual Locations.

Physical Locations are observed as an internal location that are actually part of your warehouses. 

Partner Locations,  it is the place within a customer or vendor’s warehouse. It also works like the principles of Physical                                       locations with the difference that you are not considered as the owner of the warehouse.

Structure of the Odoo 17 Analytics

1. Analytical Accounts

  • Definition: Analytical accounts are used to monitor specific costs and revenues associated with different projects, departments, or activities within a business.
  • Functionality: Each analytical account can be linked to various transactions, allowing for detailed tracking of income and expenses.


2. Analytical Plans

  • Definition: An analytical plan is a structured approach to managing and distributing costs across different analytical accounts.
  • Functionality: After setting up an analytical plan, users can modify the distribution percentages to allocate costs effectively among various accounts.


3. Analytical Distribution Models

  • Definition: These models automatically apply specific distribution criteria to transactions based on predefined rules.
  • Functionality: They help in distributing incoming and outgoing account moves across multiple analytical accounts, ensuring that financial data is accurately reflected in the respective accounts

Introduction of Dynamics Cheque Printing

Purpose – Generate cheque printout for each bank wise using bank template

This module main focus is to generate cheques through the Odoo system without manual intervention. Therefore, system user will able to post the vendor/supplier transaction and get the output of that transaction in desired bank cheque book.

According to given bank cheque sequence number system will generate its cheque output, Hence those vendor name, amount, and will vary with bank name. Therefore, we have to create different cheque layout each bank wise.

 

How to setup bank cheque layout?

Open Invoice App -> Configuration -> Cheque

Create new cheque layout with suitable height and width of each bank layout with millimeters.

 



Details of parameters

Cheque Format – Name of the bank cheque template

Cheque Dimension

Cheque height – Height of the cheque in mm

Cheque width – Width of the cheque in mm

A/C Pay

A/C Pay – Tick marks enable means printed in cheque as A/C pay cheque

Top Margin – Starting point

Left margin – left side starting point

Font Size – Size of the font

Cheque Date

Left Margin – Left side starting point

Width – breadth of the date

Font Size – Size of the font

Amount in figure

Top Margin – Starting point from top side

Left Margin – Left side starting point

Width – breadth of the date

Font Size – Size of the font

Amount in Word

No.of words of first line – number of words in first line

Company Signature

Signature box

Salutation of the 1st Signatory

Left margin – left position of the third signature starts                        

 

 

 

 

How to print a cheque for vendor payment?

First of all we have to set the cheque layout/template for different banks at initial point before it calls for the cheque.

Eg: Here I want to pay a vendor 100/- as an example.

Go to invoice -> Vendors -> Payments

Then create the new payment

 

In here we have to fill

Payment type – send since it goes out

Vendor – Vendor name

Amount – amount in cheque

Date – Cheque date

Memo – transaction text

Journal – as payment

Payment method – cheque

Cheque Number – will automatically appear next number

Vendor Bank account – if required

Then confirm the details we input.at the same time it will posted means change the draft stage to posted stage.

 


Same time we have to see journal entries generated from the system up to now.



 

Next step is we have to click on “Print cheque “button. Then system will ask bank layout to print and select the desired bank to print the cheque.




  

Final step is print the button to view the output.
